title: Knowledge management in agentic systems Part 1: Foundations – New Celent report alert
excerpt: Authored by Craig Beattie, Principal Architect & Technology Advisor at Celent, the report is the first of a four-part series on knowledge and memory in agent...
content_html:
Douglas Blakey

Wed, August 12, 2026 at 3:55 AM CDT 2 min read

Celent has published a new report, entitled Knowledge Management in Agentic Systems — Part 1: Foundations.
Part 1 of the four-part series lays the conceptual groundwork the rest of the series builds on. Specifically, it covers what "knowledge" actually means for an AI agent. And why treating it as one thing rather than four — procedural, semantic, episodic, organisational — is the most common design mistake that Celent notes in its research. It examines the working difference between retrieval-augmented generation and its graph-based variant, GraphRAG, and the layered memory architecture (working, episodic, semantic, procedural) that determines whether an agent's behaviour holds up in production or degrades into inconsistency.

It closes with the strategic argument that gives the series its throughline: model capability is commoditising quickly, and the durable competitive advantage sits in the knowledge and context layer a firm builds around it — which is why the report series argues for model-agnostic architecture from the outset.

Why this topic, what is Celent's angle?

Beattie observes that every institution he speaks with — regardless of vertical — is now running some version of the same conversation. That is, which model to adopt, and how to evaluate the next one when it arrives six months later. Almost none of them are asking the more durable question, which is what they're building underneath the model that will still be valuable when today's model is obsolete. Beattie argues that it is that the knowledge layer, not the model, that is the asset worth architecting deliberately, and that most current agentic AI deployments are brittle precisely because they've skipped that step.

The strategic conclusion is a direct challenge to how most firms currently frame their AI investment. Models are commoditising fast. A well-governed knowledge layer compounds in value the longer it runs and the more it is used. The firms that recognise this now — and build accordingly — will own something in two or three years that a competitor cannot simply buy off the shelf.

Future instalments examine knowledge graphs and regulatory representation by industry vertical, the deployment evidence from named financial institutions, and the vendor landscape for agentic memory infrastructure.

The report will especially be of interest to CIOs, CTOs, enterprise architects, and heads of AI/data strategy — across wealth management, banking, insurance, and capital markets.

content_html_zh:
道格拉斯·布莱基

2026 年 8 月 12 日星期三，美国中部时间 (CDT) 凌晨 3:55 阅读 2 分钟

Celent 发布了一份新报告，题为代理系统中的知识管理 — 第 1 部分：基础。这个由四部分组成的系列的第 1 部分奠定了该系列其余部分的概念基础。 具体来说，它涵盖了“知识”对于人工智能代理的实际含义。 为什么将其视为一件事而不是四件事（程序性、语义性、情景性、组织性）是 Celent 在其研究中指出的最常见的设计错误。 它检查了检索增强生成及其基于图的变体 GraphRAG 和分层内存架构（工作、情景、语义、程序）之间的工作差异，该架构确定代理的行为是否在生产中保持不变或退化为不一致。

它以战略论点结束该系列的主线：模型能力正在快速商品化，持久的竞争优势位于公司围绕它构建的知识和背景层中——这就是为什么该报告系列从一开始就主张与模型无关的架构。

为什么这个话题，Celent的角度是什么？

贝蒂观察到，与他交谈过的每个机构——无论垂直领域如何——现在都在进行相同对话的某种版本。 也就是说，采用哪种模型，以及六个月后下一个模型出现时如何评估。 他们几乎没有人问更持久的问题，即他们在模型下构建的东西在今天的模型过时时仍然有价值。 Beattie 认为，值得刻意构建的资产是知识层，而不是模型，而当前大多数代理人工智能部署之所以脆弱，正是因为它们跳过了这一步。

这一战略结论对大多数公司目前如何构建人工智能投资提出了直接挑战。 模型正在快速商品化。 管理良好的知识层运行时间越长、使用越多，其价值就会增加。 现在认识到这一点并相应地进行建设的公司将在两三年内拥有竞争对手无法简单购买现成的东西。

未来的文章将研究垂直行业的知识图谱和监管代表、指定金融机构的部署证据以及代理内存基础设施的供应商情况。

该报告尤其会引起财富管理、银行、保险和资本市场领域的首席信息官、首席技术官、企业架构师和人工智能/数据战略负责人的兴趣。

有关如何访问完整报告的更多信息，请访问此链接。
